configuration.title: WinForms Designer
untrusted.description: Rendering a designer loads and executes the project's control assemblies (constructors / OnPaint run on preview), so the extension is disabled in untrusted workspaces.
config.autoOpenDesigner.description: Automatically open the WinForms designer when a form's `.cs` (one that has a generated `.Designer.cs` partner) becomes the active editor — mirroring Visual Studio, where opening `Form1.cs` shows the designer. Use **View Code** to switch a form back to its `.cs` text (auto-open won't re-hijack it until you reopen the file). Disable this to keep the C# text editor and open the designer manually via **WinForms: Open Designer** or *Reopen Editor With…*.
config.assemblyPath.description:
Explicit path to the project's built control assembly (`.dll`) used to resolve custom/3rd-party controls. Leave empty to auto-discover the project's build output. Set this only when auto-discovery fails (e.g. multi-target, a custom `OutputPath`, or a not-yet-built project).

- A leading `~` expands to your home directory; a relative path resolves against the workspace folder (or the file's own directory when no folder is open). Environment variables (`%VAR%`, `${env:VAR}`, `$VAR`) are **not** expanded.
- If the resolved path does not exist, a warning is shown and auto-discovery is used instead.
- **The assembly is loaded and its control constructors / `OnPaint` run when a designer is previewed**, so it is honored only in a trusted workspace.
config.placementSnapOverrideModifier.des: Modifier key that temporarily disables move/resize snaplines for the current drag gesture. Default: Alt. Set to Disabled to always keep snapping on.
config.toolbox.autoDiscoverProjectContro: Automatically discover toolbox-eligible controls in this workspace's project build-output directories. Discovery starts only after a designer opens, runs off the activation path with file/depth/time budgets, and watches only directories that produced controls. Scan and budget details are written to the WinForms Designer output. Disable this to use only the engine baseline and controls added through Choose Toolbox Items.
config.net48.probeDirectories.descriptio:
Additional directories the **.NET Framework (net48)** engine searches when a control's assembly cannot be found — for a 3rd-party control SDK installed outside your project's build output and not registered in the GAC. Most projects need nothing here: the project's own output directory is always searched.

- Use absolute paths (a leading `~` expands to your home directory). Directories that do not exist are ignored.
- Applies to the net48 engine only, and takes effect after **Reload Window** (the engine reads them when it starts).
- **Assemblies found here are loaded and their control constructors / `OnPaint` run when a designer is previewed**, so this is honored only in a trusted workspace.
config.deleteFormSiblings.description: Delete a form's generated files together with the form. `Form1.cs` is only part of a form: `Form1.Designer.cs` and `Form1.resx` (plus any `Form1.<culture>.resx`) exist solely for it, and this extension already shows them nested under it. Deleting the form removes those files in the **same operation**, so it is one confirmation and one undo. Files that are not generated for the form — including a `.resx` whose middle segment is not a culture — are never touched. Turn this off to delete only the file you selected.
config.net48.isolateRenderWindows.descri: Run the **.NET Framework (net48)** preview engine on a private desktop that is never displayed, so a form cannot put windows on your screen while it is being designed. The compiled preview realizes the REAL form, so its own `Load`/`Shown` code runs — a splash screen, a docking panel or a dialog opened there used to appear next to VS Code. Rendering is unaffected. Turn this off only to diagnose a vendor control that misbehaves off-desktop; those windows then become visible again. Takes effect after the preview engine restarts (**Restart the Designer Preview Engine**, or **Reload Window**).
config.net48.releaseOnFocusLoss.descript: Release the .NET Framework build output every time VS Code loses focus. Mostly superseded: `winformsDesigner.net48.releaseOnExternalBuild` (on by default) already hands the output back when a build outside VS Code is about to overwrite it, and builds started inside VS Code release it themselves. Keep this off unless something else outside VS Code replaces files in the output directory — a checkout, an installer, a sync tool — since a write your open designer blocks produces no event for the build detector to see. Off by default: releasing unloads the preview, so the next edit waits for the assembly graph to load again (seconds, on a DevExpress form).
config.net48.releaseOnExternalBuild.desc: Automatically release the .NET Framework build output when a build started OUTSIDE VS Code (Visual Studio, an external MSBuild) is about to overwrite it, so that build is never blocked by the open designer with MSB3027 "The file is locked by WinFormsDesigner.Engine.Net48". Only acts while a .NET Framework designer is open and an assembly is actually being written; the previews are view-only until the build lands, then re-render from it.
config.language.description:
Language of the WinForms Designer user interface — the designer surface, property grid, toolbox, dialogs and messages. This is chosen **here**, in the extension settings; it does **not** follow the VS Code display language automatically. Default: **English**.

- Changing this takes full effect after **Reload Window** (you'll be prompted).
- Note: the VS Code **command palette** titles (e.g. *WinForms: Open Designer*) and this settings page itself follow VS Code's own *Display Language*, not this setting — a platform limitation.
